claims.title: Kingdom of Mauretania and Volubilis
claims.summary: The Amazigh kingdom of Mauretania emerges in the western Maghreb; Volubilis, founded around the third century BCE, becomes one of its leading cities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-300bce-kingdom-of-mauretania-and-volubilis, claim TL:MAR:event:300bce:kingdom-of-mauretania-and-volubilis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Roman annexation of Mauretania
claims.summary: Rome annexes the kingdom of Mauretania and the emperor Claudius organises the western part as the province of Mauretania Tingitana, governed from Tingis (Tangier).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-40-roman-annexation-of-mauretania, claim TL:MAR:event:40:roman-annexation-of-mauretania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Volubilis flourishes as a Roman city
claims.summary: Volubilis reaches its height as a thriving provincial city, adorned with a basilica, triumphal arch, temples and elaborate mosaics before Rome withdraws from the interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-217-volubilis-flourishes-as-a-roman-city, claim TL:MAR:event:217:volubilis-flourishes-as-a-roman-city, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Idris I and the founding of the dynasty
claims.summary: Idris ibn Abdallah, a sharif fleeing Abbasid persecution, wins the allegiance of the Awraba Berbers near Walila and founds the Idrisid dynasty, Morocco's first Muslim state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-788-idris-i-and-the-founding-of-the-dynasty, claim TL:MAR:event:788:idris-i-and-the-founding-of-the-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Idris II founds Fez
claims.summary: Idris II establishes Fez as his capital; it becomes a leading political and religious centre of the western Islamic world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-808-idris-ii-founds-fez, claim TL:MAR:event:808:idris-ii-founds-fez, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of the Qarawiyyin
claims.summary: The mosque and centre of learning of al-Qarawiyyin is established in Fez, later regarded as one of the oldest continuously operating institutions of higher education in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-859-foundation-of-the-qarawiyyin, claim TL:MAR:event:859:foundation-of-the-qarawiyyin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Almoravids found Marrakesh
claims.summary: The Almoravids establish Marrakesh as the capital of an empire uniting Morocco and the western Sahara under a reformist Islamic banner.

claims.title: Almoravids enter al-Andalus
claims.summary: Yusuf ibn Tashfin leads the Almoravids into Spain, checking the Christian Reconquista and bringing Muslim al-Andalus under Moroccan rule.

The Art of the Almoravid and Almohad Periods (ca. 1062–1269)

claims.title: Almohads capture Marrakesh
claims.summary: The Almohads under Abd al-Mu'min take Marrakesh, supplanting the Almoravids and building an empire across the whole Maghreb and al-Andalus.

sources.label: North Africa: The Maghrib under the Almoravids and the Almohads

claims.title: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
claims.summary: A Christian coalition decisively defeats the Almohads in Spain, beginning the dynasty's decline and reopening al-Andalus to the Reconquista.

sources.label: The Art of the Almoravid and Almohad Periods (ca. 1062–1269)
North Africa: The Maghrib under the Almoravids and the Almohads

claims.title: Fall of the Almohads
claims.summary: The Marinids capture Marrakesh, ending Almohad rule and inaugurating a new Berber dynasty centred on Fez.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-1269-fall-of-the-almohads, claim TL:MAR:event:1269:fall-of-the-almohads, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Marinids master Morocco from Fez
claims.summary: Having taken Fez in 1248 and Marrakesh in 1269, the Marinids rule Morocco from Fez, endowing the city with famous madrasas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-1269-marinids-master-morocco-from-fez, claim TL:MAR:event:1269:marinids-master-morocco-from-fez, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of the Three Kings
claims.summary: The Saadian sultan Abd al-Malik annihilates the invading Portuguese army of King Sebastian near Ksar el-Kebir; three kings die, and Morocco's independence is preserved.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-1578-battle-of-the-three-kings, claim TL:MAR:event:1578:battle-of-the-three-kings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Saadian conquest of Songhai
claims.summary: Ahmad al-Mansur sends an army across the Sahara that defeats the Songhai Empire at Tondibi, extending Saadian reach toward the gold of the Niger.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-1591-saadian-conquest-of-songhai, claim TL:MAR:event:1591:saadian-conquest-of-songhai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alaouite dynasty unifies Morocco
claims.summary: Moulay al-Rashid reunites Morocco and establishes the rule of the Alaouite dynasty, which continues to reign today; his successor Moulay Ismail builds a strong centralised state from Meknes.

claims.title: Moroccan-American Treaty of Friendship
claims.summary: Morocco and the United States conclude a treaty of peace and friendship, recognised in 1786, making Morocco one of America's earliest treaty partners.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Morocco
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Treaty of Fez establishes the protectorates
claims.summary: Sultan Abd al-Hafid signs the Treaty of Fez, making Morocco a French protectorate; a Spanish zone in the north and south and an international zone at Tangier are settled the same year.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Morocco
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Battle of Annual and the Rif War
claims.summary: Abd el-Krim's Riffian fighters destroy a Spanish army at Annual and proclaim a Republic of the Rif; a Franco-Spanish coalition suppresses the rebellion by 1926.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-1921-battle-of-annual-and-the-rif-war, claim TL:MAR:event:1921:battle-of-annual-and-the-rif-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: France deposes and exiles Sultan Mohammed V, an act that inflames the independence movement and unites Moroccans behind the monarchy.

claims.summary: Mohammed V adopts the title of king, formalising the modern Moroccan monarchy as the country builds its independent institutions.

claims.title: The Green March
claims.summary: King Hassan II leads the Green March, in which about 350,000 unarmed Moroccans enter the Western Sahara to assert Morocco's claim as Spain withdraws; the territory's status remains disputed.

claims.title: Accession of Mohammed VI
claims.summary: Mohammed VI succeeds Hassan II and undertakes gradual reforms, including a revised family law code and major development projects.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Morocco: From Berber Mauretania and the Idrisids to the Alaouite kingdom of the far Maghreb.", terralore.co/country/MAR/chronicle#ev-1999-accession-of-mohammed-vi, claim TL:MAR:event:1999:accession-of-mohammed-vi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitutional reform
claims.summary: Following Arab Spring protests, a new constitution approved by referendum expands the powers of parliament and the prime minister and recognises Tamazight, while the king retains ultimate authority.
